title: Beatrix and the Oath Anew
premise: Wren Sandoval has spent years dosing herself with poison as the crown's food-taster, but when the Thornfell border wards collapse on the night every star vanishes from the sky, she discovers her immunity was never training — it was inheritance. The blood of the ward-smiths runs in her veins, and the dying wards have been feeding on it, which means she alone can rekindle them. Guided by Halric Vane, a disgraced ward-keeper who once loved her mother, Wren must smuggle the last ember of the old oath through occupied mountain passes before the starless dark births the thing that was sealed beneath Thornfell. In the end she learns the wards demand a willing life freely given: Halric offers his own, and Wren, choosing love over duty for the first time, refuses to let him die alone — together they forge a new oath that returns the stars at the cost of everything they were.
about_author: Theo Ishikawa is a former line cook turned novelist who writes fantasy steeped in kitchens, borders, and the quiet heroism of service workers. They live in a coastal town where they keep bees and an unreasonable number of annotated maps.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A routine tasting in the royal kitchens reveals poison laced into the king's stew — poison Wren survives without effort, unsettling even herself. She pockets a vial of the residue and lies to the steward about it. Emotional beat: competence masking a growing dread that her body knows something her mind does not.

chapters.title: Roads Through Thornfell
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sent to escort a supply caravan over the smuggler roads, Wren notices the mountain wards flickering like guttering candles. An old waystone speaks her family name as she passes. Emotional beat: homesickness for a childhood she barely remembers, sharpened by the sense of being watched by the stones themselves.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At a border inn, every star goes out at once; hours later the great ward-towers fall with a sound like a struck bell. Riders pour through the gap. Wren saves the innkeeper's daughter using reflexes she never learned. Emotional beat: terror transmuting into purpose as the world's oldest protection dies overhead.

chapters.title: What the Ward-Keeper Knew
chapters.summary: Halric's POV. Halric Vane, exiled for falsifying ward-records twenty years ago, recognizes the collapse pattern instantly — it matches the forged ledgers he was forced to sign. He rides toward Thornfell to find whoever the wards were secretly bonded to. Emotional beat: guilt finally given somewhere to go.

chapters.title: Blood in the Ember
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Captured by retreating ward-soldiers, Wren is brought to a half-dead captain who touches her hand to a ward-ember and watches it blaze. 'The smith-blood,' he whispers. She flees into the mountains carrying both the ember and the accusation. Emotional beat: identity cracking open under unbearable light.

chapters.title: An Inheritance of Ash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sheltering in her abandoned family hold, Wren finds her mother's hidden workshop: ward-diagrams written in blood-ink, and a letter unfinished — 'If you are reading this, the oath has found you.' Emotional beat: grief reframed as legacy; anger at a mother who chose secrecy over safety.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Bargain
chapters.summary: Halric's POV. Halric catches up to Wren on the pass road and offers passage through occupied territory in exchange for the ember. She tests him with a poisoned cup out of habit; he drinks knowingly. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other, trust built from mutual damage.

chapters.title: Occupied Vale
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pair moves through a valley town under invader occupation, witnessing conscription and burned granaries. Wren heals a ward-scarred child with a touch, exposing them both. Emotional beat: the war stops being abstract; duty acquires faces.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Lies
chapters.summary: Halric's POV. Halric confesses his exile: he discovered the crown had been siphoning ward-strength from bonded families — including Wren's — and signed the cover-up to save his daughter. Emotional beat: shame offered honestly, and Wren's cold fury at the throne she serves.

chapters.title: Court of Cinders
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Summoned back to the capital, Wren stands before the king, who reveals he has known about the smith-blood all along and orders her to the deep vaults as a living battery. Emotional beat: love of country curdling into betrayal; the first open choice between crown and conscience.

chapters.title: Escape from the Vault
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Chained in the ward-vaults beside other drained bond-heirs, Wren uses her taster's knowledge of toxins to disable her guards and frees the survivors. One stays behind so the others can run. Emotional beat: leadership born unwillingly; survivor's guilt as fuel.

chapters.title: The Thing Beneath Thornfell
chapters.summary: Halric's POV. Scouting ahead, Halric witnesses what the falling wards unsealed: a star-devouring presence waking in the mountain's roots, wearing the shapes of the dead. He barely escapes with his mind intact. Emotional beat: dread made flesh; the stakes become cosmic rather than political.

chapters.title: Refuge at the Waystones
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The freed bond-heirs regroup at a living waystone grove where the stones teach Wren the old oath's grammar through shared memory. She sees her mother's final act: splitting the ember to hide it inside her unborn child. Emotional beat: forgiveness arriving too late to be spoken aloud.

chapters.title: A Crown's Long Arm
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Royal hunters corner the group; Halric bargains with the pursuing commander — his old forger's partner — buying time at the cost of naming himself traitor openly. Emotional beat: sacrifice as redemption's first installment.

chapters.title: The Poisoner's Art
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. To cross a warded checkpoint, Wren poses as a food-taster for the enemy general and slowly poisons his wine over three days while memorizing their deployment maps. Emotional beat: her despised skill becomes her sharpest weapon; power and self-loathing entwined.

chapters.title: Stars in Her Hands
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The stolen ember fragments within Wren begin to burn through her veins; the grove warns that carrying it much longer will consume her. She and Halric admit what has grown between them on the road. Emotional beat: tenderness against a deadline; love named plainly at last.

chapters.title: The Oath Anew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the ruined heart-tower, they learn the truth: the wards require a willing life, freely given, permanently bound. Halric steps forward before Wren can speak. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized — duty asks for one life; love refuses to pay it alone.

chapters.title: What Halric Gave
chapters.summary: Halric's POV. Halric binds himself to the tower, buying the mountain one night of restored light as the devouring thing rises. His last words to Wren are instructions disguised as a farewell. Emotional beat: grief and awe; a coward's arc completed into courage.

chapters.title: The Devouring Dark
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With Halric fading, Wren defies the oath's terms: instead of one life, she offers the shared memory of every bond-heir she freed, weaving their collective willing gift into a new kind of ward. Emotional beat: defiance of the old law; invention born of refusal.

chapters.title: Rekindling
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POV. The new oath ignites — not a wall this time, but a web linking every willing heart in the vale. The devouring thing is unmade into ordinary night, and the stars return one by one over Thornfell. Emotional beat: catharsis; the sky itself answering a choice made together.

chapters.title: After the Light Returns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The crown offers Wren honors and a gilded cage; she declines, sending the king her mother's ledger instead. Halric survives, half-bound to the tower, visiting her in the lowlands each season. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; love choosing its own shape outside of duty.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Oath Anew
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Wren's POV. Years later, Wren runs a school for bond-heirs in the rebuilt vale, teaching children that oaths are grown, not imposed. A student asks why the book of the old order was called Beatrix; Wren smiles, saying some names are seeds. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed — memory passed forward as hope rather than burden.
